original_question: Let M̃ be the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M̃ : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?
target_in_paper: §7.1, Question 13: the open problem asking whether the one-dimensional uncentered classical Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator is continuous on the normalized Banach space BV(ℝ). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful formulation: it is one-dimensional, continuous (not discrete), classical Hardy–Littlewood (not fractional), uncentered, posed on BV(ℝ), uses the normalized BV norm involving f(-∞), and asks exactly for continuity of M̃: BV(ℝ) → BV(ℝ), which is the scope of Question 13. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
missing_details: Write the operator explicitly: M̃f(x) = sup_{x∈I} (1/|I|)∫_I |f(y)|dy, with the supremum over intervals I ⊂ ℝ containing x. The paper defines the uncentered maximal operator via averages over balls containing x; in one dimension these are intervals. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
State that the functions are real-valued (the paper adopts this convention globally) and that M̃ acts on locally integrable data. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

Define the normalization term f(-∞) = lim_{x→-∞} f(x); the paper emphasizes that the full BV norm, not only the variation seminorm, is part of the question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
Make explicit that continuity means norm continuity in this Banach-space topology, i.e. if f_j → f in BV(ℝ), then ‖M̃f_j − M̃f‖_{BV(ℝ)} → 0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

Say that this is the continuous, uncentered, classical endpoint continuity problem, to avoid drifting to the centered, fractional, or discrete variants that the paper treats separately nearby. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
refined_question: Let M̃ be the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, defined for real-valued locally integrable functions f on ℝ by M̃f(x) = sup_{x∈I} (1/|I|)∫_I |f(y)|dy, where the supremum is taken over all intervals I ⊂ ℝ that contain x. Let BV(ℝ) be the Banach space of real-valued functions of bounded total variation endowed with the normalized norm ‖f‖_{BV(ℝ)} := |f(-∞)| + Var(f), where f(-∞) := lim_{x→-∞} f(x). Is M̃ continuous as a map BV(ℝ) → BV(ℝ) with respect to this norm? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1912.04625 is not a theorem or conjecture but §7.1, Question 13. The paper first recalls the endpoint W^{1,1} continuity result for the uncentered operator (Theorem 7.2), then introduces the normalized BV(ℝ) norm and immediately asks Question 13 for the uncentered operator and Question 14 for the centered one. The boundedness backdrop for even posing Question 13 is supplied earlier by the one-dimensional variation estimates for the uncentered operator in §3.1, and Table 1 later records the exact uncentered-classical / continuous-setting / BV-continuity box as OPEN. Your draft already imports almost all of that surrounding context, so it is substantially more stand-alone than the paper’s own one-line formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
